findings.doc_quote: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 30 seconds.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/config/models.py:335 — `shutdown_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, gt=0)`; the constant `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10` is defined in the same file, directly above its docstring at line 36
findings.explanation: The default per-hook bound is 10 seconds. The 30-second figure matches `startup_timeout_seconds` (models.py:328), a different setting.
findings.suggested_fix: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 10 seconds.

findings.doc_quote: A stop whose hook timed out is reported STOPPED with a "timed out" reason, even when the hook ended as soon as it was cancelled.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/app_lifecycle_instances.py:275-292 — `timed_out = force_terminated or outcome.result is ShutdownResult.TIMED_OUT`; `if outcome.is_restart_safe and not timed_out:` is the only branch that sends STOPPED. Otherwise `settle_failed_stop(...)` runs, followed by `send_outcome_event(inst, status=FAILED, previous_status=STOPPING, exception=exc)`. Lines 377-382 record the failure with `TimeoutError(... timed out after ...)`.
findings.explanation: A timed-out hook produces a FAILED outcome, a recorded registry failure and a FAILED event, even when nothing is left running. The instance stays reloadable in that case.
findings.suggested_fix: A stop whose hook timed out is reported FAILED with a "timed out" reason, even when the hook ended as soon as it was cancelled.

findings.doc_quote: A hook that catches and swallows the cancellation keeps its app stopping until its stage's deadline, then Hassette force-terminates the app.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/operations.py:184-186 — `# a hook that caught its cancellation and returned leaves the block without a TimeoutError` / `if scope.expired(): raise ShutdownHookTimedOutError(timeout_message)`. tests/unit/resources/lifecycle/test_shutdown_coordinator.py:59-71 pins this: a hook using `contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)` gets `ShutdownResult.TIMED_OUT`.
findings.explanation: The claim holds only for a hook that keeps running after catching the cancellation. A hook that catches it and returns is recorded as TIMED_OUT straight away, and teardown continues with no force-termination. The wait until the deadline comes from continuing to run (operations.py:163-165), not from swallowing alone.
findings.suggested_fix: A hook that catches the cancellation and keeps running keeps its app stopping until its stage's deadline, then Hassette force-terminates the app.

findings.doc_quote: Before the shutdown hooks run, Hassette cancels all bus subscriptions created via self.bus , all scheduled jobs created via self.scheduler , and all background tasks tracked by self.task_bucket .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/base.py:631-638 — `_shutdown_body` awaits `run_hooks(self, [self.before_shutdown, self.on_shutdown, self.after_shutdown], ...)`, then `_run_post_hook_shutdown_stage()`. That stage cancels the TaskBucket first (base.py:479), then shuts down children (base.py:507). Listeners and jobs are removed in those children's hooks: src/hassette/bus/bus.py:184-189 and src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:185-188.
findings.explanation: The order is reversed. Subscriptions, jobs and task_bucket tasks are all still live while the app's shutdown hooks run, and are cleaned up afterwards. A handler or job can therefore still fire during on_shutdown.
findings.suggested_fix: After the shutdown hooks complete, Hassette cancels all bus subscriptions created via self.bus, all scheduled jobs created via self.scheduler, and all background tasks tracked by self.task_bucket.

findings.doc_quote: attempting to override any of them raises CannotOverrideFinalError when the app is first instantiated.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/base.py:52,85 — `FinalMeta.__init__` runs when the class is created and does `raise CannotOverrideFinalError(method_name, origin_name, subclass_name, suggested_alt, loc)`; src/hassette/utils/app_utils.py:159 catches it during the load-only precheck
findings.explanation: The metaclass raises when the class is defined, so the error appears on import, before any instance exists. Line 50 of the same page correctly says class load time.
findings.suggested_fix: attempting to override any of them raises CannotOverrideFinalError at class load time.

findings.doc_quote: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.to_thread
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/app/app.py:310-335 — `await self.task_bucket.run_in_thread(self.on_initialize_sync)` and the matching calls for the other hooks; src/hassette/task_bucket/task_bucket.py:312 — `def run_in_thread(self, fn, *args, **kwargs)`. `grep -rn "def to_thread\|\.to_thread\b" src/hassette/task_bucket src/hassette/app` returns no matches.
findings.explanation: TaskBucket has no `to_thread` method. The hooks run through `run_in_thread`, which uses the dedicated sync executor.
findings.suggested_fix: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.run_in_thread

findings.doc_quote: The .sync facades provide synchronous access from _sync hooks: self.bus.sync , self.scheduler.sync , self.api.sync , and self.states.sync .
findings.code_evidence: Facades exist at src/hassette/bus/bus.py:158, src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:151 and src/hassette/api/api.py:262 (`self.sync = self.add_child(...)`). In src/hassette/state_manager/state_manager.py, a grep for `sync` matches only `after_initialize`. `self.states.sync` falls through to `__getattr__(self, domain)` at line 311, which treats `sync` as a domain name and returns a `DomainStates` type.
findings.explanation: StateManager has no sync facade. `self.states.sync` is looked up as a state domain called `sync`, so calling facade methods on it will not work.
findings.suggested_fix: The .sync facades provide synchronous access from _sync hooks: self.bus.sync, self.scheduler.sync, and self.api.sync.

summary: Seven claims failed out of 47 checked; initialization, failed-init cleanup and hook-order claims all held, and errors cluster in shutdown timing and API names on lines 23-29, 42 and 51. Caller should triage this first: six of the seven findings (all but line 25) appear only in this briefing's page text, because `docs/pages/core-concepts/apps/lifecycle.md` (clean git tree) already has the correct 10 seconds, FAILED, 'After the shutdown hooks complete', 'at class load time', `run_in_thread` and no `states.sync`, and `git log -S` on those lifecycle.md wordings (checked for all but the STOPPED one) finds no past commit.
